base_revenue.note: Total revenue FY2024 ($M) — record year for Ford

revenue_growth.note: Flat — consensus revenue forecast -0.7% to +0.8% p.a.; auto cyclical with EV transition headwinds

fcff_margin.note: Adjusted FCF $6,700M / Revenue $184,992M = 3.62%. Auto industry — low margin, high capex. Industrial segment only (excludes Ford Credit)

wacc.note: Sector WACC: Cost of equity 10.45% (Rf 4.18% + β 1.46 × ERP 4.23%) × 83.55% E-weight + after-tax cost of debt 3.97% × 16.45% D-weight

terminal_growth.note: Below US GDP — auto is mature/cyclical, no real long-run growth

net_debt.source: 10-K FY2024 Industrial segment (excludes Ford Credit financing debt)
net_debt.note: Industrial cash ~$28,500M - Industrial debt ~$20,000M = -$8,500M (net cash). Excludes Ford Credit's $137B financing debt which is offset by receivables. Pure industrial DCF only

tax_rate.note: Estimated effective tax rate — auto industry typical 12-18%

buyback_yield.note: Ford preserves cash for EV transition + dividend (~5% yield). Modest buybacks ~$1B/yr offset by SBC — net ~0% share change.

sbc_pct_revenue.note: SBC ~$0.3B / Revenue $185B = 0.2%. Auto/industrial — primarily cash comp, minimal equity.

expected_output.tolerance_rationale: Hand DCF (industrial only, g=0%) → ~$23. Market trades ~$11 — prices EV transition risk, China competition, Ford Credit drag. Wide range covers both. Below $8 or above $35 = math bug. Note: Ford is hard to DCF cleanly due to dual-segment structure (industrial + Ford Credit).
